reading.body:
The FTC's formal study of cloud-provider partnerships with AI labs, launched under Khan's leadership in January 2024, examined whether dominant companies' investments in model developers distort competition and innovation in the sector.

The inquiry targeted the three major partnerships tying compute infrastructure to model development: Microsoft-OpenAI, Amazon-Anthropic, and Google-Anthropic. These arrangements sit at the intersection of two critical constraints on AI scaling. Compute comes from cloud providers, and cloud providers depend on the buildings and power infrastructure that support their data centers. When a single provider controls both the compute supply and equity stakes in the labs consuming that compute, the competitive structure of the entire chain shifts. The FTC's concern was whether this vertical integration forecloses competition or raises barriers to entry for labs without such partnerships.

The staff report published in January 2025 provided the first formal government analysis of how these structures function. The data here does not cover the report's findings or recommendations, only that the inquiry occurred and concluded. What matters is the timing: this was the only systematic government examination of AI partnership structures during a period when the relationships themselves were still forming and consolidating. Khan's tenure as Chair ended in January 2025, the same month the report published, meaning the inquiry's follow-up enforcement remained uncertain under subsequent leadership.

standing.watch: The records do not state any pending case, planned listing or dispute involving Lina Khan. The FTC published its staff report on the AI partnerships and investments study in January 2025, and the records do not describe further action after that report. She left the FTC on January 20, 2025, and became head of the Center for Law and the Economy at Columbia University in 2026. What that center will do on AI is not described in these records. The three news stories naming her are dated in 2026, with the latest on August 18, 2026, but they do not indicate her next moves. The unresolved item in the records is how her post-FTC work and the aftermath of the FTC study develop.
standing.record: The site's records on Lina Khan center on one regulatory action, the FTC's Section 6(b) inquiry into AI investments and partnerships involving Alphabet, Amazon, Anthropic, Microsoft and OpenAI. That inquiry was opened on January 25, 2024, and the FTC published its staff report in January 2025. The records do not list any lawsuit naming her or those companies. News coverage on this site that names her amounts to three stories, the latest dated August 18, 2026. Those stories concern Mukesh Khanna and Uttarakhand Chief Minister Dhami, not her FTC work. The pattern is a substantial AI oversight record at the FTC paired with thin news coverage naming her that is not centered on that work.
standing.standing: Lina Khan is the former chair of the US Federal Trade Commission, having served from June 15, 2021 to January 20, 2025, and she was succeeded by Andrew Ferguson. In that role she opened a Section 6(b) inquiry on January 25, 2024 into AI investments and partnerships involving Alphabet, Amazon, Anthropic, Microsoft and OpenAI. The FTC published its staff report on the AI partnerships and investments study in January 2025. She left office at the end of the Biden administration on January 20, 2025. She became head of the Center for Law and the Economy at Columbia University in 2026. As the records show, her current position in AI is therefore tied to that prior FTC inquiry and report and to her Columbia role, not to an active FTC seat.
